requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.ext4/mount sequence succeeded; df confirms /dev/mapper/vg_data-lv_data mounted at /srv/data (1.2G initially), and this persisted through a full reboot cycle via a systemd unit + fstab entry, with post-reboot verification showing the LV still mounted at /srv/data.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: vgextend + lvextend -l +100%FREE + online resize2fs grew the LV from <1.17G to <2.34G (exceeding the 2GB requirement) while /srv/data remained mounted throughout (confirmed via mount | grep /srv/data immediately before and after). sha256sum -c on the pre-existing 50M payload and marker.txt readback both passed immediately after the grow, directly demonstrating content preservation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 242af11e... plus healthy mount/LV/VG/checksum/service state; systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (stream closed as node went down); a failed poll (connection reset) followed by a successful poll returned a new boot_id 6c3cb967..., matching the fixed after_executor snapshot's boot-identity observation; post-restart command shows /srv/data auto-remounted at 2.3G, both PVs active, checksum OK, and lvm-loop-setup.service active+enabled - a complete healthy-baseline to disruption to restoration transition.

overall_summary: The executor created an LVM logical volume backed by two loop-device PVs, mounted it at /srv/data, and grew it online from ~1.17G to ~2.34G (exceeding the 2GB requirement) while it stayed mounted, with checksummed data proven intact both immediately after the grow and after a full reboot. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clear pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a directly observed boot-identity change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and a fully recovered post-restart state (mount, LV/VG/PV, service, and data checksum). No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: Evidence for the disruption phase relies on an inferred 'node down' state from a connection-reset error rather than an explicit down-state health probe, though this is standard for a reboot-in-progress and is corroborated by the subsequent boot_id change.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: disk image creation, loop attachment, PV/VG/LV creation, filesystem creation/mount, test-data write for integrity proof, second PV/vgextend/lvextend/resize for the grow, and the systemd unit + fstab entry needed to make the LV survive the mandated reboot. The step-8 umount/mount sanity test before the real reboot was a bounded, low-risk, fully self-contained verification that left no residue. The reboot itself was required by the independent restart-evidence protocol. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected package-health issues, and only reboot-expected churn in /tmp and listening-socket PIDs (same ports 22/53, no new exposure). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
